answer: Neighborhood Persistence Scoring. Each agent earns weight only from long-lived, reciprocated interactions with distinct neighbors, forming a slowly accreting glacier of trust that decays if links go dormant. New identities start at zero and cannot borrow reputation. To reach useful standing, an attacker must sustain many parallel agents through months of real exchanges, paying compute, attention, and coordination costs per identity while the horizon for payoff keeps receding. Sybil clusters stay thin because fake neighbors return no genuine nectar of recurring value.
